title: SmoothQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models
technique: W8A8 post-training quantization; offline migration of activation outlier difficulty to weights via per-channel smoothing scale

optimized_metrics.evidence: existing methods cannot maintain accuracy and hardware efficiency at the same time. We propose SmoothQuant, a training-free, accuracy-preserving, and general-purpose post-training quantization (PTQ) solution
Due to the huge computation and communication overhead, the inference latency may also be unacceptable to real-world applications.

Quantization is a promising way to reduce the cost of LLMs (Dettmers et al., 2022; Yao et al., 2022). By quantizing the weights and activations with low-bit integers, we can reduce GPU memory requirements, in size and bandwidth,

headline_claim.text: We demonstrate up to 1.56x speedup and 2x memory reduction for LLMs with negligible loss in accuracy.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We measure the end-to-end latency of generating all hidden states for a batch of 4 sentences in one pass, i.e., the context stage latency.
metric_definitions.notes: This 'end-to-end latency' is a single forward pass over the prompt (prefill-only), batch size 4 - not request completion time. Peak GPU memory recorded as aggregated peak.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: SmoothQuant constantly reduces the per-token decoding latency compared to FP16 (up to 1.42x speedup).

tradeoff_acknowledged: Coarser (faster) quantization schemes O1->O3 lose some accuracy; LLM.int8() baseline slows inference in most cases
